subject.title: [Feature]: claude-cli runtime should consume per-agent auth profiles for turn auth (multiple subscription accounts on one gateway)

question: Should claude-cli turn identity be owned by OpenClaw’s selected per-agent auth profile when present, or remain gateway-global through Claude Code’s native login?
rationale: The choice determines credential precedence, token refresh ownership, subprocess secret exposure, and whether existing native-login deployments change behavior; source inspection cannot establish that product and security boundary safely.

options.title: Profile-Owned Turns
options.body: An explicit or ordered compatible agent profile overrides native login for that child, with native login retained only as the no-profile fallback and status reporting derived from the same resolver.

options.title: Gateway-Global Claude Login
options.body: Keep claude-cli authentication tied to its native shared login and update status output and documentation so per-agent OpenClaw profiles are not presented as effective for this runtime.

recommendation.title: Profile-Owned Turns
recommendation.body: An explicit or ordered compatible agent profile overrides native login for that child, with native login retained only as the no-profile fallback and status reporting derived from the same resolver.

likelyOwner.reason: This candidate has the strongest available history signal for Anthropic runtime direction and can coordinate the product choice with the credential-handling reviewers.
